newsitem.title: USA: Deutsche's Cartellieri - dlr gain unrelated to EMU.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche's Cartellieri - dlr gain unrelated to EMU.

text.p: Deutsche Bank AG Management Board member Ulrich Cartellieri said on Tuesday that the dollar's gain against the mark in recent months was not related to worries about the launch of European monetary union (EMU).
Speaking at a conference on international finance, Cartellieri said "until now there is not any indication that the current strength of the dollar is due to expectations about monetary union."
He said rather that the dollar's gains are due to expectations of higher U.S. interest rates.
Cartellieri said some foreign exchange traders have blamed the mark's decline on worries about how EMU will affect the German economy.
Cartellieri added that he expected Germany to meet the criteria for joining monetary union but "it will be a walk on a razored edge."
He said, however, it was questionable that Italy is ready for EMU.
Italian export industries would have difficulty living with a currency as strong as the mark and Rome would be hard pressed to bring its budget deficit down, he said.
